Synthetic decision-model assumptions: the fixed cost is in arbitrary normalized units, not a source-derived price. The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. Installing and proof-testing sensors is the experimental investment proposal; the source does not itself prescribe this complete installation-and-test specification. A demand means a leak-detection demand within the proposed E-001 sensor coverage. Success means delivery of the intended leak indication within that coverage. There are exactly two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes per demand: successful delivery of this specified function, or unavailability of this function. For this exercise, unavailability means that the specified function is not successfully delivered on demand, including failure to perform it; this is an operational definition, not a general equivalence of reliability and availability. The decision concerns the next 100 eligible demands after the proposed action is in place; their occurrence rate is not specified. Reliability applies only to this function and does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk.
